tickets.title: Ticket 1 — Calculate Total Daily Sales
tickets.description:
A retail store records the value of every purchase made during the day. At the end of business hours, the store manager needs to calculate the total sales amount.

Your task is to read the number of transactions followed by the transaction values and calculate the total sales for the day.

Some transactions may represent refunds, which are recorded as negative values and should be included in the final total.

Your task is to read the number of request IDs followed by the request IDs themselves and determine how many requests were successful (even) and how many failed (odd).

Output the number of successful requests first, followed by the number of failed requests.

Your task is to read the number of servers followed by their processing capacities and determine the second-highest unique capacity.

If all servers have the same capacity or there is only one server, no backup server can be selected. In that case, output **-1**.

If every record ID is greater than or equal to the previous one, print **YES**. Otherwise, print **NO**.

tickets.title: Ticket 20 — Locate a Product in the Warehouse Catalog
tickets.description:
A warehouse maintains its product catalog in **ascending order of Product IDs** so that items can be located quickly. When a customer places an order, the warehouse management system must efficiently determine whether the requested Product ID exists and identify its storage position.

Since the Product IDs are already sorted, checking every product one by one would be inefficient. Instead, implement an efficient search that repeatedly divides the search space in half.

Your task is to find the **index (0-based)** of the requested Product ID. If the Product ID is not present in the catalog, print **-1**.

**Scenario:**
An e-commerce warehouse stores all Product IDs in sorted order. Given the sorted catalog and a Product ID requested by a customer, determine the position of that product as quickly as possible.

tickets.title: Ticket 21 — Identify the First Batch Containing a Defective Product
tickets.description:
A manufacturing company maintains a **sorted list of product inspection records**. Each record contains a defect code, and multiple consecutive products may share the same defect because they were produced in the same manufacturing batch.

When a quality issue is reported, engineers need to determine **the first product** that exhibited the defect so they can identify the earliest affected production batch.

Since the inspection records are sorted by defect code, the engineering team wants an efficient solution instead of scanning every record.

Your task is to find the **index (0-based)** of the **first occurrence** of the given defect code using **binary search**. If the defect code is not present, print **-1**.

**Scenario:**
A quality assurance system stores inspection records in sorted order. Given the sorted defect codes and a target defect code, determine the position where that defect first appeared.

tickets.title: Ticket 22 — Identify the Last Batch Containing a Defective Product
tickets.description:
A manufacturing company maintains a **sorted list of product inspection records**. Each record contains a defect code, and multiple consecutive products may share the same defect because they were produced in the same manufacturing batch.

After identifying when a defect first appeared, the quality assurance team now needs to determine **the last product that contains the same defect**. This helps engineers understand the complete range of affected products before the manufacturing process returned to normal.

Since the inspection records are sorted by defect code, the engineering team wants an efficient solution instead of scanning every record.

Your task is to find the **index (0-based)** of the **last occurrence** of the given defect code using **binary search**. If the defect code is not present, print **-1**.

**Scenario:**
A quality assurance system stores inspection records in sorted order. Given the sorted defect codes and a target defect code, determine the position where that defect was reported **for the last time**.

tickets.title: Ticket 23 — Count Total Defective Products in Inspection Records
tickets.description:
A manufacturing company maintains a **sorted list of product inspection records**, where each record contains a defect code assigned during quality inspection. Since products are inspected in batches, the same defect code may appear multiple consecutive times.

After identifying the **first** and **last** occurrence of a defect, the quality assurance team now needs to determine **how many products are affected by that defect**. This information is used to estimate recall size, replacement costs, and production impact.

Since the inspection records are sorted, the engineering team wants an efficient solution instead of scanning every record.

Your task is to determine the **total number of occurrences** of the given defect code in the inspection records. If the defect code does not exist, print **0**.

**Scenario:**
A quality assurance system stores inspection records in sorted order. Given the sorted defect codes and a target defect code, determine how many products were found with that defect.

tickets.title: Ticket 24 — Find the Highest Affordable Product Price
tickets.description:
An e-commerce platform maintains a **sorted list of product prices** in ascending order. Customers often specify a maximum budget when searching for products. If there isn't a product priced exactly at the customer's budget, the platform should recommend the **most expensive product that does not exceed the budget**.

Since the product prices are already sorted, the recommendation engine must find the answer efficiently instead of checking every product.

Your task is to determine the **highest product price that is less than or equal to the customer's budget**. If every product costs more than the customer's budget, print **-1**.

**Scenario:**
A shopping website stores product prices in sorted order. Given the sorted prices and a customer's maximum budget, recommend the most expensive product the customer can afford.

However, due to an automated scheduling system, the warehouse list may start from any warehouse instead of the one with the lowest stock.

Your task is to identify the warehouse that has the **lowest inventory**, as it should be restocked first.
